title: [finding] Auth email locale reads the i18n catalog language, but a second axis (`localization.locale`) is already keyed exactly like the template rows
body:
Surfaced while implementing #8195 (PR #9134). Filed unassigned, observation-class — the shipped behaviour is correct for the four locales we ship, so nothing is broken. What is worth a decision is whether the source the ruling named is the one this should keep reading.

## What the #8195 ruling named, and what it actually returns

The 2026-08-13 ruling said recipient locale comes from the deployment default via `II18nService.getDefaultLocale()`. Measured during implementation, that method carries the **message catalog** language, whose English spelling is the bare `'en'` (`FileI18nAdapter`: `options.defaultLocale ?? 'en'`).

`sys_email_template` rows are keyed `'en-US'`, and `SendTemplateInput.locale` is documented as matched **exactly** — the contract states "no language-only prefix matching".

Passed through raw, the commonest deployment of all would therefore miss every row, fall back to the en-US body, **and still hand `'en'` to the render filters** — #7801's row-locale-vs-render-locale split reopened one notch narrower.

## How #9134 resolved it

`normalizeAuthEmailLocale` promotes a **bare language subtag** to the regional row we ship (`en`⇒`en-US`, `zh`⇒`zh-CN`, …) and passes **everything else through untouched** — deliberately, because an unshipped regional tag like `en-GB` or `fr-FR` may be a tenant's own overlay row, and swallowing it would recreate this same bug from the fifth locale onward.

That is an adaptation between two value spaces, not a change of source, so it was treated as an implementation detail rather than a re-adjudication. Reasonable, and it is pinned in both directions in `auth-email-locale.test.ts`.

## The residual question — which axis is authoritative

There is a **second** axis, found while measuring and not known when the ruling was made:

| | value space | default |
|:--|:--|:--|
| `II18nService.getDefaultLocale()` | catalog language, bare subtag (`en`) | `'en'` |
| the `localization.locale` **setting** | a select whose four options are **byte-identical to the template locale set** | `en-US` |

The setting needs no normalization at all — its option set already *is* the template row key set.

The two can disagree: a deployment whose message catalog is `zh` but whose `localization.locale` is `en-US` gets Chinese auth mail today. Whether that is right (the catalog is what the operator actually reads) or wrong (the localization setting is the declared intent) is a product judgement, not a measurement — which is why it is recorded here rather than changed.

⛔ Not proposing a switch. If the i18n service is the intended authority, the normalizer is correct and permanent, and this card closes as "answered". If `localization.locale` is the intended authority, the normalizer is a workaround for having read the other axis, and the change is a one-line source swap plus deleting the normalizer.

## Reference

- `packages/plugins/plugin-auth/src/auth-plugin.ts` — reads `II18nService.getDefaultLocale()` on `kernel:ready`
- `packages/plugins/plugin-auth/src/auth-manager.ts` — `setDefaultEmailLocale()` / `normalizeAuthEmailLocale`
- `packages/plugins/plugin-email/src/email-service.ts` — the exact-match ladder and the render-filter locale
- #8195 / PR #9134 (the ruling and its implementation) · #7801 (row locale vs render-filter locale) · #7731 (why a no-locale send resolves en-US)
